questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Communication: Meaning, Elements and Types' refers to.
questions.a: Communication is the sharing of meaning between a sender and a receiver through a message carried by a medium, completed by feedback. It may be verbal or non-verbal, formal or informal, and one-way or interactive -- and its success is judged by how far the intended meaning arrived intact.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Communication: Meaning, Elements and Types'.
questions.a: Sender, message, medium, receiver, feedback -- communication is complete only when meaning lands.

concepts.title: Media: Print, Electronic and New Media

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Media: Print, Electronic and New Media' refers to.
questions.a: Media are the channels mass communication rides on: print media such as newspapers and magazines, electronic media such as radio and television, and the new digital media of internet, e-mail and social platforms. Each has reach, cost and credibility differences that shape what it is used for.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Media: Print, Electronic and New Media'.
questions.a: Print endures, broadcast travels, digital interacts -- pick the medium that fits the message.

concepts.title: Communication Technology in Daily and Family Life

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Communication Technology in Daily and Family Life' refers to.
questions.a: Modern tools -- telephones, computers and the internet -- have changed how families study, shop, bank, work and stay in touch, and how communities access services. The chapter also flags the discipline of use: verifying information, protecting privacy and balancing screen time with real interaction.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Communication Technology in Daily and Family Life'.
questions.a: Technology multiplies contact -- and demands judgment: verify, protect, balance.
